title: Non-Hermitian Skin Effect from Radiative Coupling in a Reciprocal Chiral Medium
authors: Kin Hung Fung, Changhao Meng, Yixin Xiao, C. T. Chan
abstract: We find that long-range radiative coupling through a passive reciprocal chiral medium produces an unusual non-Hermitian skin effect in a chain of electric dipoles. Although the system is reciprocal, the chirality generates polarization-dependent phase accumulation and attenuation, leading to degenerate pairs of skin modes localized at opposite boundaries. We find that the skin mode profile consists of an exponential contribution from an isolated complex-$β$ pole and a longer-range tail proportional to $1/[n(\ln n)^2]$, where $n$ is the distance from the occupied boundary measured in lattice sites. Finite-chain calculations show that part of the OBC spectrum contracts toward the Bloch spectrum, whereas the number of boundary-localized modes remains extensive.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect in a chain of dipoles coupled via long-range radiative interactions within a chiral medium. The authors find that the resulting skin mode profile has a unique decay structure involving both an exponential pole contribution and a slower, logarithmic tail. This work advances the understanding of boundary effects in open, chiral, and long-range coupled quantum systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect (NHSE) in a system characterized by long-range radiative coupling within a reciprocal chiral medium.
main_result: The system exhibits a complex skin mode profile composed of an exponential term from a complex-beta pole and a longer-range tail decaying as 1/[n(ln n)^2].
method: The analysis involves comparing the open-boundary condition (OBC) spectrum to the Bloch spectrum using complex analysis techniques, particularly analyzing the complex-beta plane structure.
model_or_system: The model is a straight chain of electric dipoles embedded in a passive reciprocal chiral medium, whose coupling is mediated by long-range radiative interactions.
key_observables: OBC spectrum vs. Bloch spectrum, skin mode profile decay rates, and the contraction of the OBC spectrum toward the Bloch spectrum.
important_parameters: Chirality parameter (kappa), lattice site distance (n), and the chain length (N).
main_assumptions: The analysis notes that the standard equal-modulus construction is insufficient because the finite-chain decay is ultimately limited by light-line branch cuts.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Bloch spectrum versus the equal-modulus locus, show representative eigenvector amplitudes exhibiting different decay types, and compare OBC eigenvalues to the Bloch spectrum for increasing chain lengths.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon established theory of NHSE, analyzing the governing equations derived from the dipole interaction and radiative coupling. It proceeds by calculating and comparing the OBC and Bloch spectra, deriving the asymptotic decay profile, and discussing the implications of the light-line branch cuts.
why_interesting: This work extends the study of NHSE into the realm of long-range radiative coupling in chiral media, providing a detailed profile of the boundary localization that goes beyond simple exponential decay, which is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems and photonic structures.

FIG. 5. Dependence on the dissipative part of the chirality parameter, Im κ. (a) Bloch spectra of the two transverse circular-polarization subspaces. (b) Open-boundary spectra for N = 1200. Varying Im κ strongly deforms the Bloch spectrum by moving a light-line branch point, whereas the OBC spectrum remains nearly unchanged over the same range. The more visible open-chain response occurs in the directional decay of the eigenvectors.
